title: Should Equity Investors Be Reassured By Record Corporate Profits?
gist: Gavekal argues US equities are late in a 17-year bull market it explicitly compares to 1982-99, with warning signs stacking up (rising global rates, an unresolved Iran war, AI 'picks and shovels' suppliers missing inflated expectations) while investors stay calm because record post-2023 corporate profits keep P/E ratios below the 1999-2000 peak. This is a paywalled teaser that poses the question of whether that profit-based reassurance is justified but is cut off before answering it.

insights.claim: Gavekal Research characterises the current US equity advance as a 17-year bull market 'exactly analogous' to the 1982-99 run, an explicit framing that places today's market at the late, euphoric end of that historical template.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If the 1982-99 analogy is taken seriously, the reference point for the endgame is the 1999-2000 blow-off and subsequent multi-year bear market, arguing for hedging equity beta rather than adding to it.

themes.theme: Profits As The Last Line Of Reassurance

insights.claim: US corporate profits have grown phenomenally since the AI revolution began in early 2023, and that earnings growth — confirmed by another record-breaking Wall Street earnings season that ended in early August 2026 — has kept price-to-earnings ratios below their 1999-2000 peak levels.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The bull case now rests on the E rather than the P: any earnings disappointment re-rates valuations toward 1999-2000 territory without prices even falling.
insights.quote: has kept price-to-earnings ratios reassuringly below their peak levels of 1999-2000
insights.locator: This seemingly unstoppable trend, confirmed by yet

insights.claim: Gavekal frames record corporate profits as only a 'seemingly' unstoppable trend and poses whether equity investors should actually be reassured by them, signalling scepticism that the profit boom is a durable fundamental support — though this teaser is cut off before the argument is made.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Flags margin/earnings quality as the variable to stress-test in US equity models rather than the multiple, which is the consensus worry.

themes.theme: Cracks In The AI Capex Trade

insights.claim: The suppliers of 'picks and shovels' to the AI gold rush are not meeting their exaggerated financial expectations, according to Gavekal — a deterioration in the part of the AI complex that has carried the market.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Argues for trimming AI-infrastructure/semis exposure where numbers are priced for perfection; the disappointment is in delivery versus expectations, not in AI adoption itself.
insights.quote: the purveyors of “picks and shovels” to the artificial intelligence gold rush
insights.locator: Many investors have now accepted that warning

insights.claim: Gavekal lists rising global interest rates and an Iran war that has not ended as neatly as expected as two live warning signs for financial markets, and notes its own prior call that the war's end would rotate capital out of US assets has not played out as cleanly as assumed.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A messier Iran outcome plus upward-trending global rates delays the anticipated rotation out of US assets while raising the discount rate applied to them — watch long-end yields as the trigger.
insights.quote: the Iran war has not ended as neatly as many of us expected
insights.locator: Many investors have now accepted that warning

insights.claim: Investors sitting on large accumulated gains are showing few signs of serious nervousness or even discomfort despite acknowledging that warning signs are flashing, which Gavekal treats as a positioning/complacency risk in itself.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Acknowledged-but-unhedged risk is the classic setup for a disorderly de-risking; cheap convexity on US equity downside is the expression.
insights.quote: are showing few signs of serious nervousness or even discomfort
